newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch sugar beet unscathed by cold snap.
newsitem.headline: Dutch sugar beet unscathed by cold snap.

text.p: Recent cold weather across northern Europe has caused only minimal disruption to this season's Dutch sugar beet crop, the country's leading grower said on Monday.
"We've had some problems in the north of the country with night frost but in general the crop is okay," said Alfons Calon, agricultural affairs director at Cosun, previously known as Suiker Unie.
He said that from the estimated total of 115,000 hectares devoted to sugar beet in the country, some 2,500 to 3,000 hectares would have to be re-drilled.
Plantings nationwide had been completed around a week ahead of normal, and recent rains had improved crop prospects, Calon said.
"We will have a normal yield this year," he said.
Cosun produces close to 65 percent of Dutch sugar beet.

The Institute for Sugar Research (IRS) has said it plans to issue the first computer-generated crop forecast of the season -- used in the Netherlands in place of traditional sugar beet tests -- in August.
